The IC metric relies on human-annotated S_q, which affects both the automation of the evaluation process and its consistency, as differences in annotation standards across annotators may impact reliability.\n\n4. The lack of ground truth forces the evaluation of search results to depend heavily on LLM-as-Judge (e.g., IA@k), which raises concerns about evaluation cost, especially for multi-turn agentic search scenarios."}},"parentInvitations":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/-/Official_Review","nonreaders":[],"tmdate":1762916543406,"tcdate":1761794835806,"writers":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference","ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission3082/Reviewer_29uc"],"signatures":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission3082/Reviewer_29uc"],"forum":"snm8tq7sdI","number":2,"license":"CC BY 4.0","cdate":1761794835806,"readers":["everyone"],"invitations":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission3082/-/Official_Review","ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/-/Edit"],"mdate":1762916543406,"domain":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference","replyto":"snm8tq7sdI","id":"BpAoQTSb29","forumContent":{"venue":{"value":"Submitted to ICLR 2026"},"TLDR":{"value":"We introduce InfoDeepSeek, a new benchmark with challenging questions and fine-grained evaluation designed for assessing agentic information seeking in real-world, dynamic web environments."},"keywords":{"value":["Search Agent","Large Language Model"]},"primary_area":{"value":"datasets and benchmarks"},"abstract":{"value":"Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding responses with retrieved information. As an emerging paradigm, Agentic RAG further enhances this process by introducing autonomous LLM agents into the information seeking process. However, existing benchmarks fall short in evaluating such systems, as they are confined to a static retrieval environment with a fixed, limited corpus and simple queries that fail to elicit agentic behavior. Moreover, their evaluation protocols assess information seeking effectiveness by pre-defined gold sets of documents, making them unsuitable for the open-ended and dynamic nature of real-world web environments. To bridge this gap, we present InfoDeepSeek, a new benchmark with challenging questions designed for assessing agentic information seeking in real-world, dynamic web environments. We propose a systematic methodology for constructing challenging queries satisfying the criteria of determinacy, difficulty, and diversity. Based on this, we develop the first evaluation framework tailored to dynamic agentic information seeking, including fine-grained metrics about the accuracy, utility, and compactness of information seeking outcomes. Through extensive experiments across LLMs, search engines, and question types, InfoDeepSeek reveals nuanced agent behaviors and offers actionable insights for future research"},"_bibtex":{"value":"@misc{\nxi2026infodeepseek,\ntitle={InfoDeepSeek: Benchmarking Agentic Information Seeking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation},\nauthor={Yunjia Xi and Jianghao Lin and Menghui Zhu and Yongzhao Xiao and Zhuoying Ou and Jiaqi Liu and Tong Wan and Te Gao and Bo Chen and Weiwen Liu and Yasheng Wang and Ruiming Tang and Yong Yu and Weinan Zhang},\nyear={2026},\nurl={https://openreview.net/forum?id=snm8tq7sdI}\n}"},"title":{"value":"InfoDeepSeek: Benchmarking Agentic Information Seeking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation"},"pdf":{"value":"/pdf/ff9ab890884f04a4657bccc19d078e4987004270.pdf"},"venueid":{"value":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission"},"paperhash":{"value":"xi|infodeepseek_benchmarking_agentic_information_seeking_for_retrievalaugmented_generation"},"authorids":{"value":["~Yunjia_Xi1","~Jianghao_Lin1","~Menghui_Zhu2","~Yongzhao_Xiao1","~Zhuoying_Ou1","~Jiaqi_Liu20","~Tong_Wan2","~Te_Gao1","~Bo_Chen17","~Weiwen_Liu1","~Yasheng_Wang1","~Ruiming_Tang2","~Yong_Yu1","~Weinan_Zhang1"]},"authors":{"value":["Yunjia Xi","Jianghao Lin","Menghui Zhu","Yongzhao Xiao","Zhuoying Ou","Jiaqi Liu","Tong Wan","Te Gao","Bo Chen","Weiwen Liu","Yasheng Wang","Ruiming Tang","Yong Yu","Weinan Zhang"]}},"version":2},{"content":{"summary":{"value":"This paper introduces a novel LLM routing paradigm, an agentic router setting. Unlike traditional routers, the proposed GraphPlanner not only selects the backbone LLM but also assigns specific agentic roles, e.g., planner, executor, or summarizer, to solve the initial query. The router is parameterized by GARNet, a graph-based model that captures the relationships between queries, agentic roles, and responses. GARNet is optimized using PPO with a joint loss that balances task-specific performance and computational costs, enabling adaptive router learning. Extensive experiments across 14 diverse tasks, spanning in-domain and out-of-domain settings, as well as inductive and transductive scenarios, demonstrate GraphPlanner's SOTA performance, exceptional balance of cost and performance, and strong generalization capabilities."},"soundness":{"value":3},"confidence":{"value":3},"questions":{"value":"Please refer to Weaknesses part"},"rating":{"value":8},"code_of_conduct":{"value":"Yes"},"presentation":{"value":3},"contribution":{"value":3},"strengths":{"value":"1. The proposed agentic router setting is well-motivated and clearly articulated. While traditional single-round routers are limited to solving isolated queries and multi-round routers can only model sequential workflows, GraphPlanner addresses more complex graph-structured workflows that are under-explored in prior work.\n\n2. GraphPlanner is designed with sound principles, featuring a lightweight implementation and effective contextual history preservation. This ensures that the agentic router is simple to implement and extend. Additionally, the joint optimization of the router, combining task-specific loss and cost constraints, allows the model to learn policies tailored to solved task while maintaining efficiency.\n\n3. The experimental results are extensive, covering a wide range of downstream tasks in both in-domain and out-of-domain scenarios. The authors also include detailed cost-performance trade-offs and further analysis in inductive and transductive settings. These results highlight GraphPlanner's SOTA performance compared to single-round and multi-round routers, its robustness in inductive and out-of-domain tasks, and its favorable balance between performance and computational costs.\n\n4. The paper is well-written, with vivid figures and tables that significantly enhance comprehension."},"flag_for_ethics_review":{"value":["No ethics review needed."]},"weaknesses":{"value":"1. The description of Phase 1 optimization is somewhat unclear. For instance, in the case of Depth = 1 and Width = 3, does this imply a fixed agentic workflow where the first step always involves an initial planner role, followed by two roles (e.g., summarizer or executor)? Further clarification of this process would be helpful.\n\n2. The paper lacks illustrative examples showing how the router assigns roles to specific models to successfully solve queries. Including such examples would better demonstrate how GraphPlanner operates in practice.\n\n3. The experimented datasets appear relatively simple, as single-round routers already achieve good performance in some scenarios. It would be valuable to test GraphPlanner on more challenging benchmarks, such as agent-related benchmarks, which involve complex workflows and are better suited for role decomposition."}},"parentInvitations":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/-/Official_Review","nonreaders":[],"tmdate":1762933700258,"tcdate":1760691817687,"writers":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference","ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission20197/Reviewer_SiqR"],"signatures":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission20197/Reviewer_SiqR"],"forum":"ZdGB7MNQDT","number":1,"license":"CC BY 4.0","cdate":1760691817687,"readers":["everyone"],"invitations":["ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission20197/-/Official_Review","ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/-/Edit"],"mdate":1762933700258,"domain":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference","replyto":"ZdGB7MNQDT","id":"o2t6C4H7zd","forumContent":{"TLDR":{"value":"GraphPlanner is a graph memory-augmented framework that enables multi-agent LLM routing by modeling cooperation and memory with reinforcement learning, achieving scalable, efficient, and generalizable routing."},"venue":{"value":"ICLR 2026 Poster"},"keywords":{"value":["Multi-agent LLMs","Memory utilization","Heterogeneous agents","Graph"]},"primary_area":{"value":"learning on graphs and other geometries & topologies"},"abstract":{"value":"LLM routing has achieved promising results in integrating the strengths of di-\nverse models while balancing efficiency and performance. However, to support\nmore realistic and challenging applications, routing must extend into agentic LLM\nsettings—where task planning, multi-round cooperation among heterogeneous\nagents, and memory utilization are indispensable. To address this gap, we pro-\npose GraphPlanner, a heterogeneous graph memory-augmented agentic router\nfor multi-agent LLMs that generates routing workflows for each query and sup-\nports both inductive and transductive inference. GraphPlanner formulates\nworkflow generation as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where at each step\nit selects both the LLM backbone and the agent role (Planner, Executor, Sum-\nmarizer). By leveraging a heterogeneous graph, denoted as GARNet, to capture\ninteraction memories among queries, agents, and responses, GraphPlanner\nintegrates historical memory and workflow memory into richer state represen-\ntations. The entire pipeline is optimized with reinforcement learning, jointly\nimproving task-specific performance and computational efficiency. We evalu-\nate GraphPlanner across 14 diverse LLM tasks and demonstrate that: (1)\nGraphPlanner outperforms strong single- and multi-round routers, improv-\ning accuracy by up to 9.3% while reducing GPU cost from 186.26 GiB to\n1.04 GiB; (2) GraphPlanner generalizes robustly to unseen tasks and LLMs,\nexhibiting strong zero-shot capabilities; and (3) GraphPlanner effectively\nleverages historical memories, supporting both inductive and transductive infer-\nence for more adaptive routing. Our code for GraphPlanner is released at\nhttps://github.com/ulab-uiuc/GraphPlanner."},"_bibtex":{"value":"@inproceedings{\nfeng2026graphplanner,\ntitle={GraphPlanner: Graph Memory-Augmented Agentic Routing for Multi-Agent {LLM}s},\nauthor={Tao Feng and Haozhen Zhang and Zijie Lei and Peixuan Han and Jiaxuan You},\nbooktitle={The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations},\nyear={2026},\nurl={https://openreview.net/forum?id=ZdGB7MNQDT}\n}"},"title":{"value":"GraphPlanner: Graph Memory-Augmented Agentic Routing for Multi-Agent LLMs"},"pdf":{"value":"/pdf/17611e5cf01588da0763474eada151c274fe2695.pdf"},"venueid":{"value":"ICLR.cc/2026/Conference"},"paperhash":{"value":"feng|graphplanner_graph_memoryaugmented_agentic_routing_for_multiagent_llms"},"authorids":{"value":["~Tao_Feng5","~Haozhen_Zhang1","~Zijie_Lei1","~Peixuan_Han1","~Jiaxuan_You2"]},"authors":{"value":["Tao Feng","Haozhen Zhang","Zijie Lei","Peixuan Han","Jiaxuan You"]}},"version":2},{"content":{"venue":{"value":"CoRR 2014"},"pdf":{"value":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1403.3758v3"},"venueid":{"value":"dblp.org/journals/CORR/2014"},"paperhash":{"value":"besse|big_data_retour_vers_le_futur_3_de_statisticien_à_data_scientist"},"authorids":{"value":["https://dblp.org/search/pid/api?q=author:Philippe_C._Besse:","https://dblp.org/search/pid/api?q=author:Aurélien_Garivier:","~Jean-Michel_Loubes1"]},"html":{"value":"http://arxiv.org/abs/1403.3758"},"_bibtex":{"value":"@article{DBLP:journals/corr/BesseGL14,\n  publtype={informal},\n  author={Philippe C.
